newsitem.title: USA: Challenger Gray sees large drop in April job cuts.
newsitem.headline: Challenger Gray sees large drop in April job cuts.

text.p: U.S. companies have decreased the number of jobs they were cutting nearly 70 percent, the lowest level in four years, said Challenger, Gray & Christmas Inc, an outplacement firm.

Some 15,214 job cuts were announced in April, a 69.7 percent drop from March when 50,182 cuts were announced, the firm said. The April figure was a 50.6 percent drop from April of 1996, indicative of a tight labor market.

"The fact that job cuts dropped so dramatically while at the same time hiring was lower than expected in April is evidence that the country is at virtually full employment," said John Challenger, executive vice president of the firm.

"In a situation like this employees are likely working more overtime hours and doing jobs of two or more people," Challenger said. "Employers must now asssign more tasks than in the past since they cannot hire additional staff because of the labor shortage."
